messages:
jamie (support): ACME reported heavy tail latencies after we enabled the new 'aggressive-int8' quant profile on their dedicated pool (eu-west-2) at ~09:58 UTC. p50 flat, p95/p99 doubled. customer provided a small repro and wants immediate mitigation.

alex (eng-runtime): thanks. any errors or OOMs? stack traces?

jamie (support): no errors, no OOM. metrics show CPU on host low, GPU util steady. only thing abnormal is time spent in kernels per request. I pulled three sample request IDs: rq_9a1, rq_9a7, rq_9c3.

ops-bot: deployed profile 'aggressive-int8' to pool ded-gpu-eu-west-2 at 09:56 by rollout-bot.

riley (eng-ml): jumping in. quick hypothesis: quantization introduced many dequant/quant transitions because our fused attention kernel didn't match some micro-batched sequence lengths in this workload; runtime fell back to a generic slower path that does dequant per-op. That increases host<->device transfers and kernels.

maria (sre): timeline correlates: profile flip 09:56, traffic ramp 09:57, first Slack mentions 09:59. No autoscaler activity. Disk/io normal.

alex (eng-runtime): can someone run a capture of the slow request and paste the per-step latencies?

jamie (support): pasted trace for rq_9c3 (sanitized):
```
request_id: rq_9c3
steps:
  - load_model: 12ms
  - kv_cache_lookup: 8ms
  - attention_step_1 (quant-dequant): 420ms
  - matmul_int8_fallback: 610ms
  - attention_step_2 (quant-dequant): 380ms
  - memcpy d2h: 240ms
  - finalize: 30ms
total_ms: 1800
```

riley (eng-ml): that's consistent with repeated quant-dequant + memcpy stalls. Two immediate avenues: 1) roll back that customer's mapping to fp16 to remove quant path; 2) try enabling the fused kernel path explicitly for that pool (QUANT_FUSED_FORCE=1) which avoided fallback in local repros.

alex (eng-runtime): preference is minimal blast radius. Support wants rollback now. Also need short explanation for customer. Jamie, can you push rollback and tell us when done?

jamie (support): starting rollback now (API call).

jamie (support): rollback applied at 10:07 UTC to map longform-7b -> longform-7b:fp16 for acme route.

ops-bot: route update applied to ded-gpu-eu-west-2 for customer acme-inc at 10:07 by jamie.

maria (sre): monitoring p95/p99 for that pool. Initial metrics: p95 600ms -> 420ms within 90s, p99 1800ms -> 720ms in 3m. customer reports improvement.

riley (eng-ml): good. root cause writeup (short): the aggressive-int8 profile introduced calibration bins with outlier scale values leading the kernel selector to pick a generic int8 fallback that performs dequantize on each attention/MLP op. That fallback has large memcpy and quantization overhead for these sequence shapes, producing tail latency spikes.

alex (eng-runtime): what immediate engineering mitigations? list them.

riley (eng-ml): short-term: 1) per-customer rollback to fp16 (done); 2) per-pool toggle QUANT_FALLBACK=fp16 if quant-dequant transitions per-request exceed threshold; 3) re-run calibration with percentile clipping (99.5 -> 99.0) and produce a conservative profile.

alex (eng-runtime): longer term: 1) add a kernel selection test in CI that checks for heavy fallback count on representative prompt sets; 2) add telemetry to count quant->dequant transitions and expose per-route SLO guard; 3) consider fp8 experiments (may reduce dynamic range mismatch) but needs separate calibration pipeline.

maria (sre): ops tasks we executed:
- rolled mapping to fp16 for customer route at 10:07
- set alert: if p99 > 800ms for 5m reopen incident
- added temporary dashboard to track quant-dequant counts by pool

jamie (support): customer message drafted: "We rolled your endpoints back to the fp16 variant to remove the int8 fallback path that caused tail latency spikes. We're running a targeted recalibration and additional tests and will reintroduce quantization via a canary once verified. We can also run a targeted calibration on your production prompts if you'd like." They asked for ETA for when int8 can be safely reenabled.

riley (eng-ml): ETA: calibrate on customer samples and run canary cycles ~ 4-6 hours; additional kernel selector fix and CI tests ~ 48-72 hours. FP8 quick experiment queued, not for immediate canary.

alex (eng-runtime): action items (owners + ETA):
- riley: create new profile acme_v2 with clipped calibration and test (ETA 4h)
- eng-runtime: add per-pool QUANT_FALLBACK flag + safe-gate in rollout system (ETA 24h)
- infra: add lightweight per-request quant-transition counter metric (ETA 12h)
- support: follow up with customer and offer sample calibration canary (ETA now)

maria (sre): creating incident ticket INC-2026-1428 and linking traces.

jamie (support): closing thread for now, will reopen if regression reappears. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-1428 created by maria. ticket: https://tickets.internal/INC-2026-1428
